sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Import
sections.what: Brings in the guide type that tool entries use.
sections.why: Needed so each tool can link to its guide.

sections.name: IntelligenceTool
sections.title: Tool entry shape
sections.what: Describes what each tool entry must contain: names, paths, demo and guide links, image and alt text, headline, steps, output and caveat.
sections.why: Keeps every tool entry complete and in the same shape.
sections.watch_out: A missing required field breaks any card that reads it.

sections.name: intelligenceTools (part 1)
sections.title: Yard, Reality Scan and Lessons Learnt
sections.what: Lists the first three tools with their paths, steps, outputs and caveats. The Reality Scan demo note says its recorded run covers little cost and schedule data. The Lessons Learnt demo note states project and fact counts. Also begins the Opportunity Map entry.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the user-facing copy.
sections.watch_out: Figures in the demo notes must be kept in step with the real demo data.

sections.name: intelligenceTools (part 2)
sections.title: Opportunity Map output and caveat
sections.what: Finishes the Opportunity Map entry with its output description and caveat, then closes the list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the user-facing copy.
sections.watch_out: The caveat says an inferred opportunity is only a research lead, which should stay visible.

sections.name: industryImages, assetUrl
sections.title: Industry images and base address
sections.what: Keeps a table of pictures and alt text for each industry, and builds a full image address from the app's base folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app may be served from a sub-folder, so the base address is added at run time. Otherwise reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Image paths must match real files, and the base address comes from the build setting.

sections.name: industryImage
sections.title: Industry image picker
sections.what: Looks up an industry name in lower case. Returns its picture if listed. Otherwise picks one by keywords such as nuclear, dairy, mining, renew and lng, and falls back to a refinery picture.
sections.why: Gives every industry a picture even when it is not in the table.
sections.watch_out: Keyword matching is loose, so any name containing a keyword gets that picture.

summary: The list of the app's analysis tools with their names, paths, images, steps and cautions, plus helpers that choose the right picture for an industry.
purpose: Supplies the words and pictures for the tool overview cards and pages.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The content is user-facing copy, and each tool carries its own caveat.
how: Defines the shape of one tool entry. Lists four tools: Yard, Reality Scan, Lessons Learnt and Opportunity Map. Each has names, paths, optional demo and guide links, an image with alt text, a headline, steps, an output description and a caveat. Keeps a table of industry images. Builds a full image address from the app's base folder. Picks an industry image by matching keywords, with a default.
inputs: An industry name, when picking an image.
outputs: The tool list, plus image addresses and alt text.
risks: Several demo notes contain fixed figures, such as 191 projects and 870 facts. These go stale when the data changes. The caveats are part of the product's honesty and should not be removed casually.
debug: If a tool card looks wrong, check its entry in the list. If an image is missing, check that the file exists in the image folder and that its path here matches. If a demo link fails, check its path and demo flag.
